newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Corps up with govies and stocks.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Corps up with govies and stocks.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds registered solid gains in secondary trading as well as the primary market on Wednesday, following rallies in both U.S. Treasuries and stocks, sources said.
"The Treasury market hit a low yield for the year; the stock market reached a new high; and corporate bonds are better across the board," one investment-grade trader said.
High-grade bonds tightened two to three basis points on average in healthy trading activity on Wednesday.
Junk bond issuers priced several blowout deals, while outstanding debt rose 1/4 to 1/2 of a point, traders said.
Junk bonds are up on the euphoria in the stock market (today)," one junk bond trader said.
In credit-specific news, ITT Corp made waves in the corporate bond market by announcing it plans to buy back its entire $2.0 billion in outstanding debt through a tender offer later this year.
Traders said ITT long bond spreads tightened roughly 40 basis points to 95 basis points over Treasuries on the news.
The tender offer is part of ITT's plan to split into three separate companies in order to fend off a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp.
One notable example was Nextel Communications Inc sale of exchangeable PIK preferred stock, which was increased to $500 million from an original size of $350 million.
The deal, underwriten by Morgan Stanley, was priced at par to yield a dividend rate of 13 percent.
The securities were heard trading at 102 later in the day.

Global Ocean Carriers Ltd sold $125 million in junk bonds on Wednesday, increasing its deal by $25 million. Also, Resource America Inc sold $115 million offering, hiking the deal from an original size of $75 million.

"ITT is making a good faith effort for bondholders and shareholders which is what they did in their last restructuring in 1995," said Ed Oppedisano, corporate bond analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"Obviously this is a good move for bondholders," he said.
In the junk bond market, new issues were the focus of Wednesday's activity, with most deals receiving enthusiastic receptions from investors.
Traders noted investors were digesting this week's enormous new issue calendar nicely with many deals being upsized and immediately trading better in the aftermarket.
Finally, Trico Marine Services Inc sold $110 million in senior notes on Wednesday, upping its deal from $100 million originally.
The one exception to such successful offerings was a $350 million deal from Brazilian electric utility ESCELSA which fell victim to the recent voliatily in Brazilian markets.
Morgan Stanley, its lead underwriter, postponed the deal until next week, sources said.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose above the 8,000 mark for the first time on Wednesday, surging 63 points to close at 8,039.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries rallied to their best level since December, surging after the 30-year bond yield broke the psychologically important barrier of 6.50 percent.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 28/32 to close at 101-29/32, pushing its yield down to 6.48 percent.
-Douglas Brown, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1662
